plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets in Sydney turn lilac when this tree blooms. Clusters of trumpet-shaped flowers open on bare or feathery-leaved branches, then drop to cover pavements and parked cars in a violet carpet.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with the main display from October through November
plants.funFact: The tree is native to South America, yet it has become so tied to late-spring life in Australian cities that its bloom is traditionally linked with university exam season.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen shrub brightens the cooling days of late autumn. Its delicate, often lightly scented blooms open wide to show golden stamens, and in a mild garden they keep coming into winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter, usually starting in October or November and continuing into December or January
plants.location: Southern Japan, and mild temperate gardens in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua is a close relative of the tea plant, and its seeds are pressed for an oil used in cooking and hair care in Japan.

plants.name: Schlumbergera truncata
plants.description: This rainforest cactus has no spines. Instead it has chains of flattened, pointed-toothed segments, and bright, arching flowers dangle from their tips. It flowers as the days shorten, so it brings colour indoors in late autumn.
plants.location: Native to the Atlantic Forest of southeastern Brazil, and grown as a houseplant worldwide
plants.funFact: In the wild it is an epiphyte, living on tree branches and mossy rocks rather than in desert sand.
